Yak-42 has a narrow-body fuselage with a circular cross-section and a pronounced dorsal fin extending forward from the base of the vertical stabilizer.
Yak-42 has two main landing gear units, each with four wheels arranged in a tandem bogie, located under the wings near the fuselage.
Yak-42 has a cockpit with a stepped windscreen featuring three distinct pane levels, unlike the smooth, blended curvature of modern airliners.
Yak-42 has a single pair of overwing emergency exit doors on each side, positioned just aft of the wing trailing edge.
Yak-42 has a relatively short fuselage with a steeply raked nose section that ends in a blunt, almost vertical front profile.
Yak-42 has engine nacelles that are short and cylindrical, lacking the extended bypass ducts seen on later-generation turbofans like those on the Boeing 737NG.
Yak-42 has a vertical stabilizer with a straight leading edge and a slightly swept trailing edge, differing from the highly swept fin of the Ilyushin Il-62.
Yak-42 has a forward-fuselage cross-section that tapers noticeably toward the nose, creating a wedge-like appearance when viewed from below.
Yak-42 has a main landing gear with outward-canted struts and dual-wheel bogies, visually distinct from the inward-canted gear of the Antonov An-148.
Yak-42 has a wing with moderate sweep (approximately 25 degrees) and no winglets, contrasting with the sharper sweep and wingtip devices of the Sukhoi Superjet 100.
Yak-42 has a rear fuselage that bulges outward to accommodate the side-mounted engines, producing a wider diameter than the forward fuselage.
Yak-42 has a cockpit canopy with thick, widely spaced framing bars and no integrated eyebrow windows, unlike the seamless glazing of the Embraer E-Jets.
Yak-42 has a ventral fin beneath the rear fuselage, extending downward from the base of the vertical stabilizer, absent on most Western narrow-bodies.
Yak-42 has a forward cargo door located on the left side just ahead of the wing root, distinguishable from the nose-loading configuration of the Antonov An-26.
Yak-42 has a wing with a straight leading edge outboard of the engine pylons and a noticeable kink where the pylon attaches, unlike the smoothly curved leading edge of the Yak-40.
Yak-42 has a tailcone that slopes upward sharply from the rear pressure bulkhead to meet the base of the vertical fin, forming a distinct ramp-like contour.
